children: Peter Thiel

once argued that people planning their careers should worry less about building the perfect résumé and instead ask whether they are learning now and working toward something meaningful in the long run.
Thiel Warns Against Résumé-Driven Career Planning

Speaking at the University of Texas at Austin in 2014, Thiel said people often treat careers like a "branching tree diagram," choosing graduate school, consulting or other prestigious paths because each credential appears to unlock another option rather than doing what they actually want. UT Austin hosted Thiel that year to discuss innovation and his book
Zero to One

Thiel divided career decisions into three horizons — short-term happiness and learning, medium-term résumé value and long-term meaningful work. "We are in a skewed world where we overweight the medium-term," he said, urging people to "focus on some combination of short-term and long-term and forget about the medium-term."
That advice resurfaced this week when billionaire investor and Pershing Square CEO
Bill Ackman
responded to a post quoting Thiel’s remarks with two words, stating, "Good advice."
